title: Low-degree relevant-coordinate finder
statement: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, a low-degree relevant-coordinate finder assigns to each coordinate set $P\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, each fixed sign assignment $z$ on $P$, and each failure parameter in $(0,1/2]$ a randomized program using random labeled examples and returning either no decision or a constant-sign or coordinate-split decision. It also specifies natural-number bounds on the number of random-example calls and on local work. Every outcome in the program's support uses at most the declared number of examples, makes zero membership queries, and uses at most the declared local work; moreover, for every target depending only on some coordinate set $J$ of size at most $k$, whenever $P\subseteq J$, the probability that the returned decision is absent or incorrect for the restriction fixed by $z$ is at most the given failure parameter.
hypotheses_covered: outcome lies in the program's support for the pathwise cost bounds
